entry.description: Where the phone starts: the runtime made ready for core, then Expo Router's root layout and one thin route for each Place. Expo Router reaches the routes itself, so nothing imports them

client-screens.description: What the user sees on a phone: the shell around every Place (Splash, signed-out card, header, Sidebar with the User Switcher, Local Sign-In, the Commands, and the layer gestures mount in), each Place, the Add and Accounts sheets, and the parts they share

screens.description: The shell holds the frame and opens the sheets over it; each Place is its own module a route opens, and Entries opens the Accounts sheet to rename one; all of them draw with the shared parts

client-ledger.description: Ledger's client from core, made once on the phone's platform Layer, with the theme remembered on this phone and the sounds and haptics of Commands: what every screen uses for Ledger's state, Settings, Users and Backend

client-platform.description: The phone's platform Layer core asks for: tables and Remote copies in expo-sqlite, the last User in secure storage, the network from expo-network and the foreground from AppState, and the Remote Backend's sign-in (a stub until Phase 4)

runtime.description: What Hermes lacks that core expects of a runtime, put in place before anything else loads: crypto.randomUUID and getRandomValues

ledger-expo.description: Read top-down: entry readies the runtime and routes to the screens; the screens stand on Ledger's client from core, made on the phone's platform Layer. Everything shared with the web app is in @ledger/core; generic native UI, gestures and feedback are in @kstackz/expo-toolkit
